plan: [In a second-price auction with a common value and symmetric noisy signals, the optimal bid is the conditional expectation of the common value given my signal. With my signal s=44, the prior v∈[20,29] and noise ∈[-20,20] imply v|s is uniform on [24,29]. So E[v|s]= (24+29)/2 = 26.5. I will bid 26.5.]

[My private signal is low (18). The common value is uniform 20–29, so unconditional E[value]=24.5, but winning with a low signal risks the winner’s curse: others likely have higher signals, so if I bid aggressively I may overpay. With only one round and no history to exploit, the profit-maximizing conservative choice is to avoid winning at an unfavorable signal. I will bid zero (avoid paying and avoid the winner’s curse). ]

[My observed signal S=15 gives no information about the common value C beyond the prior (C uniform 20–29), so E[C|S]=24.5. In a second-price auction with common value uncertainty, a good practical rule is to bid near the posterior mean but shade downward to reduce winner’s curse risk. I therefore choose a conservative bid slightly below 24.5 to maximize long-run expected profit while avoiding overpayment.]
